# Community plugin source and builds

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

These retained source snapshots record Muse community-plugin dependencies. [sources.json](sources.json) records each public upstream repository, version, license, and either its revision or recovered release archive SHA-256. The snapshots retain upstream source and manifests; some text files normalize CRLF to LF. Declared local modifications record original and maintained file hashes; the builder verifies maintained bytes before applying overlays and includes the record in the artifact's `SOURCE.json`. No installed profile, credentials, user media, or generated runtime is a build input. The translation gate excludes the retained upstream directories and hash-checked embedded upstream resources; Muse-owned source and documentation remain checked.

[owned-downloads.json](owned-downloads.json) separately pins the Muse Hongguo and Douyin download bundles. The inventory also includes the local [reverse tools](muse-reverse-tools/README.md) and independent [Fanqie downloader](muse-fanqie-download/README.md) and [Lvpaopao downloads](muse-lvpaopao/README.md). Their READMEs own configuration and verification limits; they do not change the retained upstream inventory.

Entries with `desktop: false` in the source inventory and archived `ds-bot` source are omitted from default builds. `dsh-plugin-subscriptions` supplies the active subscription bundle; the old Codex pin and source remain for explicit recovery builds. Desktop packaging independently selects its package closure and does not copy every available tarball. `--only dsh-plugin-subscriptions` selects the current subscription artifact; `--only dsh-codex-subscription` selects the archived compatibility path.

The unknown-assertion gate uses the [file-origin lock](../../scripts/retained-plugin-origins.json), not directory exemptions, for reviewed upstream files. Immutable files must match their pinned content hash. Maintained files also require their declared hashes and exact original text; only assertion operators and types mapped one-to-one through unchanged lines retain upstream ownership. New or changed assertion lines, unlisted files, and owned adapters remain checked. The five original-text fixtures retain the pinned Visualize [BSD-3-Clause license](dsh-visualize/LICENSE); pin updates require review of the source hashes and originals together. Source, pin, lock, original-text and license paths are checked component by component; ancestor symlinks and junctions, non-files and paths outside the canonical repository are rejected even when their content hashes match.

The older Feishu and IM source exclusions remain separate from this file-origin mechanism.

## Build

Use an installed checkout with the current Host and Client packages already built. From the repository root:

```sh
pnpm --dir third_party/plugins/toolchain run build --out ../../../.artifacts/community-plugins
pnpm --dir third_party/plugins/toolchain run test:host
pnpm --dir third_party/plugins/toolchain run test:build
pnpm --dir third_party/plugins/toolchain run test:im
```

Before running retained DS Bot source tests, install its locked runtime dependencies with `npm ci --prefix third_party/plugins/ds-bot --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --legacy-peer-deps --no-audit --no-fund`. The test resolver supplies the Harness peers from the built checkout.

[build.mjs](build.mjs) installs the separate [toolchain lock](toolchain/pnpm-lock.yaml) with frozen resolution and install scripts disabled, using its own workspace configuration to omit automatic installation of the four deep-view Host peers supplied by staging, then compiles and packs each plugin serially in temporary staging. `--only dsh-ffmpeg` selects one source directory. Staging links to this checkout's built Host packages, never a live profile. Child checks use a temporary Harness home and omit credential-bearing environment variables and inherited `NODE_PATH`, so a package-manager shim cannot expose workspace-only dependencies to artifact qualification. Subscription test preloads use file URLs so native Node accepts absolute paths on Windows as well as POSIX systems; the launcher and loader options otherwise remain unchanged. The helper removes its links before deleting staging; source directories receive no generated output or `node_modules`. The bridge's upstream JavaScript source already lives in `lib`.

Each tarball retains its upstream license and Codex notices, adds the bundled Heroicons license where needed, and records the upstream pin, reviewed Host/vendor versions, and toolchain-lock digest in `SOURCE.json`. The [Host qualification](compatibility/host-runtime.mjs) rejects unreviewed Host or vendor releases. Artifact manifests disable lifecycle scripts, pin runtime dependencies, and explicitly admit the reviewed Host and vendor prereleases in peer alternatives. They omit the retired `dsh-invariants` dependency. Build overlays leave retained manifests and source files unchanged.

The archived Codex compatibility build records its changes in `SOURCE.json`: subtask inspection and preparation accept only the reviewed Host provider version, and the CLI remains pinned to `0.153.4`. The provider and Host adapter share the Host's installed pi-ai `1.3.0`; the copied runtime and artifact peer admit that exact version. The overlay checks the retained provider module and catalog fixture SHA-256 values. Copied checks use the current model catalog and exercise custom context with GPT-5.6 Luna; removed offline models receive no invented aliases. It resolves the CLI manifest and wrapper under `app.asar.unpacked` when packaged. Retained upstream files remain unchanged; unexpected source text fails the overlay rather than silently skipping it.

The archived Codex subscription models appear in the model picker only while a Codex OAuth account is connected. Muse login does not authorize the subscription provider; disconnecting Codex hides its models on the next list request. Its model menus and sticky group headings use the theme's opaque base fill in both light and dark modes. The private staging overlay uses the shared portal and viewport placement with one pane at a time, preserves model, effort, speed and output-detail actions, and records these choices in `SOURCE.json`.

The Desktop panel also lists runtime-registered MCP tools as read-only connections. The compatibility overlay never copies credentials, environment values, or private launch arguments into the listing.

## Compatibility and Desktop integration

`dsh-skill-mcp-panel` is pinned to upstream 2.3.5. Its Web sidebar manages Skills and MCP server configuration for the active profile. The bundled artifact omits the upstream `dsh-panel` executable and disables automatic global CLI installation: Desktop launches supported Node applications only through `dsh` profiles. Activation does not invoke npm or write into the application directory; the staging checks mount the built panel against a read-only directory and retain its Skills and MCP registrations. The panel's gateway configures MCP connections; the actual MCP client remains `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`. Its retained model, gateway, slot, and icon checks run during the isolated build.

The Skill / MCP panel uses the bundled version and does not check upstream releases or display plugin update notices. Its compatibility update endpoint returns the installed version without a network request. Skill and MCP management remain available.

The Muse panel and its nested skill provider exclude the shared user `~/.agents/skills` root, including overrides from `DSH_AGENTS_HOME`. Skills installed for coding assistants there do not appear in Muse's management list or nested catalog. Muse's own user skills and explicitly referenced workspace skills remain available; shared skill files are not modified. The Host filesystem provider separately limits discovery to the product's configured roots.

The panel recognizes workspace `.muse/skills`, `.dsh/skills` and `.agents/skills` directories. Imports keep the existing global or workspace save location. After format validation and a successful file transaction, the additive result fields `status: saved` and `discovery: ready | pending | unavailable` distinguish persisted files from current conversation availability. The browser retains a localized notice for pending or unavailable discovery; it does not report a format failure or delete saved files. Actual write failures still roll back only the newly created targets from that batch. Files deleted by an older version cannot be reconstructed by this change.

The builder imports every built Host entry. The archived Codex build runs 26 retained upstream checks against the current DSH APIs and pi-ai 1.3.0, including model preparation and authenticated-carrier validation; the upstream registration context is a test double, not a full Desktop Loader. Eight additional Codex checks load the real provider, Host adapter, and CLI, exercise authenticated subscription SSE and subagent transport with simulated peers, and reject runtime-version drift and incorrect archive paths. FFmpeg runs 89 retained checks. The build tests check exported artifact files and byte-identical tarballs for every pinned plugin from two clean staging directories on the same platform. They do not establish cross-platform or whole-installer byte identity.

The archived Codex build additionally loads its artifact through the real Loader, Settings, local credentials, LLM, Web, tool and subagent providers with the optional CLI absent; it checks actual Cordis candidate-config hooks, account RPC, saved preferences across restart, disposal and zero outbound requests. A mandatory built-Client check mounts the account section and model selector with current Cordis, React, slots and primitives, exercises the login command and model selection, and verifies unload. The recorded Session scenario captures the actual subscription image tool and its refusal when no account is connected.

The [Desktop package target](../../apps/desktop/scripts/package-target.ts) builds Desktop-enabled entries from both inventories in step S6 and places their tarballs beside first-party packed inputs. [Package-set preparation](../../apps/desktop/scripts/prepare-package-set.ts) selects the [source plugin names](../../apps/desktop/src/core-package-set.ts) as explicit roots and rejects registry substitution. Desktop development also builds and stages their Desktop-enabled entries. Packaging is not activation: the release still needs a real Desktop Host/Client smoke. Account login, paid requests, and real media encoding are outside these keyless build checks.

Market's HTTP UI is not suitable for the portless Desktop carrier. The archived Codex build uses the optional connection fetch carrier rather than requiring a Web server. FFmpeg needs the product's configured encoder paths. Do not infer enabled features from a tarball's presence.

### Subscription providers

The default Desktop source inventory selects [dsh-plugin-subscriptions](dsh-plugin-subscriptions/README.md) at the MIT release pinned in [sources.json](sources.json). Its private build overlay adapts the retained Host and Client entries to the reviewed DSH runtime; installed user profiles and credentials are not build inputs. The previous `dsh-codex-subscription` source remains disabled for default Desktop builds.

The subscription runtime artifact exports JavaScript only; it does not publish TypeScript declaration files. The retained upstream TypeScript source remains unchanged. Archived recovery builds retain the old Codex native-CLI subagent path; the replacement uses ordinary DSH subagents. Old canvas, PSD, annotations and enhancement preferences are not directly migrated.

The [subscription migration guide](../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.2-rc.1/muse-subscriptions/guide.md) covers account stores, retained Session history and the old enhanced preview and annotation data. Failed imports persist `manual-login-required` for explicit login; if the marker cannot be saved, status warns that automatic import may retry after restart. New provider registration, image attachments, real account access and successful inference require separate verification; a package archive alone establishes none of these outcomes.

### Muse remote desktop and Feishu

`@wenbin_wb/dsh-bridge` retains upstream version 2.12.1 at the fixed revision in [sources.json](sources.json), including its MIT attribution. The [normalization record](dsh-bridge/MUSE_SOURCE_NORMALIZATION.json) records original and local SHA-256 values for 21 text files whose trailing whitespace or final newlines were normalized. The [reviewed overlay](compatibility/bridge-desktop.mjs) pins that record, checks each normalized file and every retained module before packing, and includes the record in `SOURCE.json`. Its Desktop artifact retains only the account tunnel modules: the old Feishu Host, Client, gateway, conversation bridge, file tools and SDK are absent. The root entry fails explicitly and directs IM consumers to `@xmanrui/dsh-im`; `./client` is absent, while `./remote` continues account-bound desktop access. The default bundle mounts the canonical native IM provider. The artifact also excludes upstream application bins, LAN proxy, standalone tunnel server, Cloudflare, self-update, and upstream password/QR authentication.

The remote provider reuses `CustomTunnelClient` connection setup and native WebSocket upgrade handling. The Muse adapter streams raw native bytes without accumulating complete frames, including Host Ping and browser Pong, and supplies account/device authentication, streamed HTTP uploads and downloads, per-chunk acknowledgements, cancellation, continued reconnects at the configured interval, and awaited shutdown. Its local transport tests cover binary uploads, Range responses, partial native frames, `/api/remote.mux` heartbeat round trips, cancellation, and rejected credentials. The handshake adds hostname and operating system to its installation UUID. The cloud relay authenticates the account and routes each browser tab to its selected installation while other computers stay connected; the desktop forwards only to its own loopback Host. This is a private outbound connection and creates no public tunnel hostname.

`@xmanrui/dsh-im` supplies native IM bot settings, Feishu streaming cards and channel management. [sources.json](sources.json) pins its MIT source. The [IM overlay](compatibility/im-desktop.mjs) builds the retained Host and Client in private staging and places a Muse importer at the root entry. Its empty bundle patch prevents a second Host connection. The previous PGZXB source remains retained with `desktop: false` and is not activated. Account remote access continues through the bridge's separate `./remote` provider.

The importer transfers enabled legacy credentials through the Host credential service and imports private bindings only after an authorized message establishes the old chat's peer. It keeps the original files and complete old message-claim ledger. Only native `dsh-im` receives Feishu messages and card callbacks; legacy migration does not authorize these events. Messages and card actions use the access policy saved in native IM settings, without additional legacy group or direct-message allowlists. Group messages still require an exact mention of that bot, and registered owners retain their native privileged access. Existing native IM bots are not overwritten. The native IM settings remain available without legacy credentials. Ordinary Muse Sessions handle incoming messages without the archived Muse Bot service. Existing chat keys, Session IDs, model selections, workspace bindings and durable message-claim and topic-reply records remain in use. See the [migration guide](../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/muse-im-channel/guide.md).

Allowed members may answer questions from tasks they initiated, including custom answers, without command permission. Other users receive an explicit notice and cannot answer that question. Management buttons still require command permission. An open group policy admits messages; it does not change the Agent's tool permissions or sandbox settings.

Each Feishu bot uses the workspace selected in its IM settings for both direct and group chats. Chats share files and materials in that directory while keeping separate Session histories. Startup removes per-chat workspace overrides and detaches bindings whose Session working directory differs from the bot workspace; matching bindings retain their Session IDs. Later conversation commands cannot restore a private directory override or bind another chat's current Session. Selecting a different bot workspace changes subsequent work for all its chats. Old Session logs and files stay in their original locations; the adapter does not move them.

The Muse wrapper and native Feishu plugin explicitly declare `sessions` and `sessionPersistence` dependencies so workspace validation can read live or persisted Session headers. The isolated IM checks exercise migration, real Loader and Agent APIs, group mentions, control ownership and restored Session history with an offline platform transport. A Cordis plugin with restricted service access creates new direct and group Sessions through the real Host gateway, with the same selected workspace and separate histories; a missing-dependency check rejects undeclared Session access before a model prompt. The build check compares two complete tarballs, verifies their native client and license, and checks that retained upstream files remain unchanged. These checks do not authenticate a live bot or establish tenant permissions.

### Ordinary-session cards

The retained [Deep View](deep-view/README.md) plugin provides `show_view` in ordinary Muse conversations. Its structured views include tables, charts, choices and forms. Interactive answers return through the owning Session; native `ask_user_question` remains available for simple questions. The source pin records the public fork and upstream revision, and the builder qualifies its Host and browser entry against the current runtime. Bot teams remain archived.

The independent [Skill evolution plugin](muse-skill-evolution/README.md) reviews newly completed tool-assisted work, creates owned Skills and retains proposals and rollback versions. Native persisted review Sessions use the task's selected model route. Its README owns review limits, normal model usage and file permissions.

The retained [Visualize](dsh-visualize/README.md) plugin renders interactive HTML cards and standalone pages. Desktop expands page views in the conversation because its shell rejects Blob popups; Web can open a separate tab. `visualize`, `show_view` and native `ask_user_question` remain resident and are omitted from Tool Search. The bundled authoring Skill is available in Muse's creative catalogs. Card buttons may fill the owning conversation's composer; the user sends the draft. Existing drafts and attachments are retained. Card updates stay within the owning Session. If saving stops after a file commit, the error receipt distinguishes the fragment and image manifest; inspect the reported path before another correction rather than repeating an old replacement blindly.

### Archived Muse Bot

[DS Bot source](ds-bot/README.md), its pinned license and the compatibility overlay remain available for archive restoration. Default builds skip it even though its upstream pin is retained; only explicit `--only ds-bot` selection enters its legacy build path. Use a separate output directory for recovery artifacts. Default builds do not delete older archives already present in an output directory.

The archived path retains its browser/Office build and `test:bot` checks; these do not activate Bot features in the ordinary-session product. Existing private Bot state and Session files remain untouched. The [ordinary-session upgrade guide](../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/muse-session-product/guide.md) covers reserved-profile backups and restoring an archived application.

### Hongguo public metadata

`muse-hongguo-search` retains the recovered 0.1.0 MIT source, [recovery record](muse-hongguo-search/RECOVERY.md), and immutable original release archive. Its original development commit was not recovered; `sources.json` pins the verified archive SHA-256. The [Host overlay](compatibility/hongguo-host.mjs) verifies a reviewed file inventory, records local metric-handling changes, adds the exact tested tools peer, and disables global activation. Standard, PTC, Cordis, Short Drama, and Editing activate the four tools in their own scopes; Minimal retains no Hongguo tools.

Search, detail, rankings, and collection filtering use public official metadata pages without a key or Cookie; no initial user configuration is required. Ranking cards with verified identities remain available when displayed metrics are missing. Each observation retains collections, likes, heat, and missing-field reasons; results report page coverage separately from metric coverage. Search covers the initial window, and rankings cover the requested public boards rather than the entire platform. Website requests remain serial, rate limited, cached, and cancellable; access restrictions fail explicitly. The plugin does not download videos. Offline regressions and real Host registration, canonical results, prompt discovery, input rejection, cancellation, and unload checks run during packaging. `test:hongguo` checks two clean, identical tarballs; live site availability is a separate read-only check.

### Qimao public metadata

The Muse-owned [Qimao plugin](muse-qimao-data/README.md) uses `parse5` to read public metadata without executing page scripts. Its scoped tools expose verified ranking windows, filtered library pages, bounded search within those results, and book details. Missing metrics remain unknown. The package retains its MIT reference attribution and enters Desktop through the owned source inventory; no registry substitution or global tool activation is required.

### Selection snapshots and reports

The Muse-owned [source research plugin](muse-source-research/README.md) calls the reviewed metadata clients and preserves their complete results in immutable, versioned workspace files. Its comparisons retain missing values, original observation times, collection scope, and metric labels. Reports identify their input snapshots and coverage; legacy files remain explicitly imported evidence.

Its work-mapping proposals bind both source references and evidence hashes to a human review. Confirmed, rejected, and deferred decisions retain their revision history. Reports may cite those decisions without inferring platform-wide absence of adaptations or sequels.

### Muse local tools

Build the owned download bundles from the repository root with the separate [builder](build-downloads.mjs):

```sh
node third_party/plugins/build-downloads.mjs --out .artifacts/download-plugins
```

Standard, PTC, Cordis, Short Drama, and Editing activate `hongguo_download_info`, `hongguo_download`, `douyin_download`, `reverse_skill`, `reverse_analyze`, `fanqie_download_info`, and `fanqie_download` inside their agent scopes; Minimal contributes none. The tools use the initiating conversation's workspace for output. Installing the tarballs with `dsh plugin --profile headless add <tarball>` activates their bundle patches in that profile; building a new Desktop release includes them through the preset compositions.

Download bundle packing accepts npm and pnpm lifecycle entries, resolves pnpm's installed JavaScript bin or Corepack launcher when the lifecycle entry is native, and disables lifecycle scripts through the package-manager environment. Node-based packers never interpret a native pnpm executable as JavaScript; Desktop process orchestration can run that executable directly without a shell. `node --test third_party/plugins/download-pack.test.mjs` verifies all owned archives through both the installed JavaScript launcher and pnpm's actual lifecycle entry, checks credential-file exclusion, and preserves source manifests. The Node tar parser reads archive members by exact Unicode paths. Reverse and Fanqie archives must contain the files declared in `SOURCE.json` with their exact SHA-256, except upstream `.gitignore` metadata excluded by npm.

Hongguo defaults to the supplied source's legacy interfaces and accepts several series IDs. The operator must supply the original `config.json`, `devices.json`, and a working signing service through the package's documented configuration. Missing source configuration fails explicitly, and public preview episodes do not establish full-series availability. Douyin accepts a list of user-selected video links, verifies each download with FFmpeg, and reports blocked or partial batches. A list of videos alone does not establish complete coverage of a drama; platform login or verification takes place in Muse's internal Browser panel, without external profiles or Cookie-file import.

Douyin preserves Session-owned download tasks across runner restarts. Its [plugin reference](muse-douyin-download/README.md) describes receipt checks, explicit recovery, and unfinished states; the [upgrade guide](../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/muse-download-tasks/guide.md) covers custom compositions and matching Desktop peers.

Lvpaopao's owned series jobs retain the existing per-episode manifest and original reconciliation keys. Its [reference](muse-lvpaopao/README.md) separates local progress from source availability; acquiring new playback information still requires a qualified logged-in WeChat runtime.

See each retained upstream license and notice before redistribution. The build preserves the Codex PSD codec notices and includes the full license of bundled Heroicons. Runtime dependencies retain their own licenses in the packaged dependency graph. Muse Med does not claim authorship or endorsement by these projects.
